title: Normal Force
body:
The **normal force** is the push a surface exerts on an object resting against it, directed
perpendicular to the surface, which is what normal means here.

It is a response force with no fixed value: it takes whatever magnitude prevents the object
from passing through the surface. That is why it cannot be assumed equal to the weight.

```
level surface, nothing else vertical:   N = mg
in a lift accelerating upward at a:     N = m(g + a)      you feel heavier
on a ramp at angle θ:                   N = mg cos θ      smaller than the weight
pressing down with an extra force F:    N = mg + F
```

The ramp case is the one used most, because the [[Free-Body Diagram]] resolves the weight
into a component along the surface, $mg\sin\theta$, which drives the slide, and a component
into the surface, $mg\cos\theta$, which the normal force cancels. Since [[Friction]] is $\mu
N$, friction on a ramp falls as the ramp steepens.

The normal force and the object's weight are not a third-law pair. They act on the same object,
which is what disqualifies them; the partner of the normal force is the object pushing down on
the surface.
